observations:
All conceptual domains in Torah #139 are fully accounted for by the three packages proposed in torah_139_packages.json. No independent bechina domain was identified that is structurally separate from the existing three packages.

The four bechina relationships found in the source text distribute cleanly into three thematic families:
  (A) Package 1 (good): מִצְוָה = קוֹמָה שְׁלֵמָה = צֶדֶק = בְּחִינַת רַגְלִין; with שַׁבָּת / יִקְרָא דְּשַׁבַּתָּא merged in by shared nature.
  (B) Package 2 (evil): קְלִפָּה = חִיצוֹנִים = 'רַגְלֶיהָ יוֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת'.
  (C) Package 3 (good): תַּעֲנוּג + דֶּרֶךְ כְּבוּשָׁה merged by shared-nature (both = God's response to the ascending mitzva).

No additional independent bechina family exists in the text. The Torah's conceptual scope is deliberately narrow: one positive cluster (the mitzva as ascending tzedek/komah), one negative cluster (the klipa as descending 'raglehah yoredot mavet'), and one culminating cluster (divine pleasure generating a communal path).

Good/evil mirror: The Torah has a precise structural mirror:
  Package 1's 'בְּחִינַת רַגְלִין לַעֲלוֹת לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ-בָּרוּךְ-הוּא' (feet ascending before God)
  mirrors
  Package 2's 'רַגְלֶיהָ יוֹרְדוֹת מָוֶת' (feet descending to death).
The raglayim-concept is the pivot concept: the same 'feet' can ascend or descend depending on who controls them — this is the crux of the teaching. Shabbat is the mechanism that transfers the raglayim from the klipa's downward pull to the mitzva's upward walk. This mirror structure is complete within the three packages; no fourth package is warranted.

Note: Torah #277 is explicitly referenced at Torah #139's conclusion ('עַיֵּן עִנְיָן זֶה לְקַמָּן סִימָן רע"ז בַּאֲרִיכוּת') as the fuller elaboration of this teaching. When Torah #277 is analyzed, its packages will likely extend and deepen the same conceptual families, potentially introducing additional bechina nodes within the mitzva-tzedek cluster or the klipa-chitzonim cluster. Any such additions will belong to Torah #277's package analysis, not to Torah #139's.
